notes.claim: One single-phase winding makes a pulsating field, not a turning one, so it gives no starting torque; a three-phase motor on one phase will not self-start but can be hand started either way.

A start winding at 90 electrical degrees, with thinner wire and fewer turns, has higher resistance and lower inductance, so its current shifts less than the main winding's; the two currents are out of step and the field turns.
The angle between the two currents in a split-phase motor is about 30 degrees.
Starting torque goes with the currents and the sine of the angle between them.
A centrifugal switch drops the start winding out: at 3/4 of synchronous speed (Kuphaldt), about 75% of running speed (his sheet), approximately 80% of full speed (MSU).

Split-phase starting torque is low and suits easily started loads and fractional horsepower, up to 1/3 horsepower (250 W); typical figures are 100 to 175% of rated torque and 700 to 1,000% of rated current.
The start winding is not rated for continuous use, so frequent starts or a long start can overheat and burn it out.
Once started the auxiliary winding is optional; the main winding alone keeps the motor running.
The direction is set by reversing the leads of one winding (start or main) before starting.

sources.quote: a type of single-phase motor that uses two stator windings—a main winding and a starting (or auxiliary) winding—displaced by 90 degrees.

sources.quote: The starting winding is made of thin wire with fewer turns, giving it a higher resistance and lower inductance.

sources.quote: Once the motor reaches about 75% of its running speed, a centrifugal switch opens to disconnect the starting winding, and the main winding sustains the motor's operation.

sources.title: 13.9: Single-phase Induction Motors
sources.quote: This coil produces a moderate starting torque, which is disconnected by a centrifugal switch at 3/4 of synchronous speed. This simple (no capacitor) arrangement serves well for motors up to 1/3 horsepower (250 watts) driving easily started loads.

sources.title: Electrical Tech Note — 313
sources.quote: This method of starting results in relatively low starting torque. Split-phase motors are suited only for fairly easy starting loads.

sources.title: Your motor sheet: the split-phase motor
sources.quote: Because of their low starting torque, they are best suited for applications with little to no initial load, such as fans, and some types of pumps and compressors.
